source_evidence: cash accounts (a brokerage account in which you must pay the full amount for any securities purchased) and margin accounts (a type of brokerage account in which your brokerage firm lends you cash, using the account as collateral, to purchase securities).
answer: A cash account requires you to pay the full amount for securities you buy. A margin account lets the brokerage firm lend you cash to purchase securities, using your account as collateral. The key difference is whether you pay the full purchase amount yourself or borrow cash from the brokerage firm.
